scope.ui: Actual compiled dist served at the native shell trusted local origin; actual main/preload/security/IPC, fresh isolated profile. Initial dev avatar warms bootstrap; this is not a cold-load test.
scope.interaction: Real panel typing, one delayed local task response driving authoritative thinking/idle, repeated open/close and rapid reversals. No mic, TTS, provider or production backend task.
scope.timing: Test-only WebGL/rAF API wrappers add overhead. Document rAF and actual avatar draw callback clocks are proxies, not OS presentation. No screenshot, video, GPU info or memory dump inside the timed interaction.
scope.resources: Created/deleted WebGL handle counts, not allocated bytes, physical VRAM or driver reclamation. The live field means created minus explicit delete, not validity after context loss. Test-held references intentionally prevent a GC claim.
scope.lifecycle: Actual compiled renderer API in a separate 96px test owner after panel timing; actual IntersectionObserver offscreen and native window hide/show; actual dispose. Native pet counts remain separate.

tiltWarmup.scope: Real pointer tilt in both directions before the measured interval; excludes first-use shader work. Compare the separately retained first-use report.

interaction.retainedDraft: Keep this unsent draft through every opening and reversal.

trace.clock: Trace ts/dur are Chromium monotonic microseconds across native processes; browser performance.now/rAF times are document-relative milliseconds. START/END TimeStamp events identify the timed window; different clock origins are not subtracted.

presentationFeedback.interpretation: Chromium emits these events with presentation_feedback.timestamp, which strengthens the rAF-only evidence. Captured events include begin-frame IDs but no hardware-clock/completion flags. These are Chromium presentation-feedback timestamps; verified OS/hardware scanout is unclaimed.

sources.limit: Current primary source; exact packaged Chromium152 source tag was unavailable to the web reader.

sources.mechanism: kHWClock and kHWCompletion distinguish hardware-origin/completion feedback from estimates; captured AnimationFrame events do not include these flags.

strictGates.p95PresentedIntervals: Chromium presentation-feedback intervals measured below; hardware-backed OS presentation remains unverified because feedback flags are absent.
strictGates.noAppCausedOver50Ms: A bounded trace with zero feedback intervals over50ms supports this run only; physical presentation and arbitrary workload attribution are unverified.
strictGates.firstResponseWithinTwoPresentedFrames: Unverified: state markers and frame IDs do not by themselves attribute the first visible pixel change to a causal input frame.

strictHardwarePresentationAcceptance: Unverified; feedback hardware flags and causal first-response pixel/frame attribution are unavailable.

resourceStability.scope: The original timed native five-cycle panel run, retained unchanged by lifecycle-only followup. A96px closed→72px expanded avatar resizes its Three transmission target; only balanced texture:FBO:RBO1:2:3 reallocation is allowed. Historical same-size exact-equality evidence remains separate and unchanged; no create/dispose-cycle or total-VRAM claim.
resourceStability.classificationScope: Endpoint texture dimensions and FBO creation-order accounting prove the bounded resize signature; intermediate dimensions and RBO storage formats are not recorded. All other cumulative counters and texture signatures remain equal. No total-VRAM claim.

memory.note: Geometry bytes describe CPU attribute storage. Environment estimate is one RGBA16F target; neither measures total GPU allocation or driver overhead.
